name: Fourier-character CE learnability matching
status: corrected before corpus profiling or natural-data training; removes the initialization-response detour
scope: architecture-conditioned prediction from dataset Fourier energy and realized held-out CE learnability
hypothesis: Natural-data held-out CE learning difficulty is predicted by the Fourier-energy-weighted empirical CE difficulty of learning the same exact characters with the same architecture.

sampling.unit: contiguous 129-byte chunk yielding 128 inputs and 128 shifted targets; bytes are never shuffled within a chunk
sampling.train_chunks: uniform with replacement over eligible starts in train blocks
sampling.profile_positions: uniform without replacement over eligible starts in profile blocks
sampling.validation_chunks: 128 fixed starts without replacement in validation blocks, identical across architectures and seeds

fourier_character_training.supports: all 63 nonempty subsets of the seven lags through degree three
fourier_character_training.target: deterministic parity, equivalently the real Walsh character, on the binary values at the support lags
fourier_character_training.data_seed_note: retains the exact random character examples used by the 270 already-completed CE-only cells; those training computations never consumed an initialization-response value
fourier_character_training.hardness: median over seeds of normalized held-out cross-entropy curve area over normalized log example count; exact Bayes floor is zero
fourier_character_training.kernel: one raw empirical CE-hardness value for every architecture and exact Fourier support; no initialization or gradient proxy

profile.basis: inverse-likelihood categorical projection under the sampled dependent data measure
profile.support_energy: positive nested-projection increments attributed to each exact unordered Fourier lag support
profile.overlap: positive Fourier-support-energy weighted empirical held-out CE character hardness

prediction.model: standardized unpenalized OLS fit to 24 pilot corpora times five architectures
prediction.continuation_gate: Fourier-CE matched grouped leave-one-corpus-out point RMSE improvement over the strong baseline is positive

decision.transfer_gate: Fourier-CE-matched minus strong-baseline paired RMSE improvement interval strictly above zero and positive point improvement for at least three of five architectures
